hero.filename: Interior of Brill car 519 in Issaquah Valley Trolley service (2014).jpg
hero.caption: Interior of Issaquah Valley Trolley car 519 loaded with passengers during a trip on the line. Car 519 is ex-Lisbon No. 519 and was built in kit form by the American J. G. Brill Company and assembled in Portugal in 1925.  One remnant of its service career in Portugal still visible here is the lettering "24 lugares" (located just to the right of the motorman), which is Portuguese for "24 seats", the car's seating capacity.

images.filename: Ex-Lisbon Brill streetcar 519 at Issaquah Depot with boarding ramp in place (2014).jpg
images.caption: Issaquah Valley Trolley Brill car 519 laying over at the Issaquah Depot terminus, with a boarding ramp in place to bridge the gap between the station platform and the car's first step.  Car 519 is ex-Lisbon No. 519 and was built in kit form by the J. G. Brill Company (of Philadelphia) and assembled in Portugal in 1925.
images.alt: Issaquah Valley Trolley Brill car 519 laying over at the Issaquah Depot terminus, with a boarding ramp in place to bridge the gap between the station platform and the car's first step.  Car 519 is ex-Lisbon No. 519 and was built in kit form by the J. G. Brill Company (of Philadelphia) and assembled in Portugal in 1925.

images.filename: Issaquah Valley Trolley carbarn - north end, with car 519 pulling in and Milan car 96 outside (2014).jpg
images.caption: The north end of Issaquah Valley Trolley's carbarn, with ex-Lisbon car pulling in (at the end of the operating day) and ex-Milan interurban car 96 being stored outside, partly covered by a tarp.  Car 96 was never operational while in Issaquah, and it was sold to a group in Oregon in 2015 (and left Issaquah in December 2016).

images.filename: Generator trailer of Issaquah Valley Trolley in 2014.jpg
images.caption: Issaquah Valley Trolley's generator trailer – a diesel (or gasoline)-powered generator mounted on a rail cart and connected with cables to car 519, supplying electricity to its motors, as the line is not equipped with overhead trolley wires.  The streetcar tows or pushes the generator trailer when in operation on the line.
